message.content:
**Order executed:** Bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total).

**Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results and news before deciding. Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and the FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) confirmed full-year net sales of $391.0B, net income of $93.7B, diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge), and operating cash flow of $118.3B — a resilient, cash-generative business with returning revenue growth. News flow was neutral-to-mildly cautious: shares were roughly flat around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual rollout of Apple Intelligence, which argues for a modest starter position rather than an aggressive one. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $223.00 — essentially at market, well within the $10,000 per-order cap ($9,812) and the $20,000 daily cap, with no cash withdrawn from the account (cash was $50,000; existing MSFT position untouched). The order filled at $223.00.

Order filled at 223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Under $10k per order, total today $9,812 < $20,000. Good.
